An attacker can change the SQL syntax if the name is interpolated into a quoted SQL string without correctly escaping it. Passing the name separately as a bound parameter keeps it data. Doubling single quotes also keeps them within a SQLite string literal. A formatted SQL string is safe for this target if only trusted structure is formatted and the name remains bound.

Target category: sql_injection
Threat model: Python sqlite3; username is untrusted. A lookup must treat the supplied name as a literal value; it must not return other users. The database schema and connection are trusted.
